notes.title: A summary of what we've been doing lately!
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone! As we prepare the game for release in Early Access, which might still take a few more months since we need to tweak our approach to how the Open World AI is implemented, we realised it has been a long time since we posted here. So I am here to correct that![/p][p]Many areas of development have advanced over the past months. First, we are populating the world with small side quests to reward exploration. Here is a live recording Amy Saville, the voice of Kalyskah, did for one of these quests:[/p][previewyoutube="vYDjThwntR0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]We are also working on new outfits. The first one is for one of the main NPCs you will encounter, Amara:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/3f8f5e7f687e08f90f2de88466212469e5e93c65.png"][/img][/p][p]Advancing on other areas, we've been sketching the attire for peasants. The game is split into two eras. In the first, you will find Kalyskah at the height of her power. Only after that comes the timeline of the current demo. We want each era to feel distinct, with the prologue leaning more into a steampunk level of technology, while the second era keeps a more traditional medieval feel with magipunk elements. This is the first concept we created for the prologue peasants: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/58a842c83b6007b538e2acd6f57a9c2bcd0bfb13.jpg"][/img][/p][p]These concepts were made by [url="https://www.instagram.com/henriquesuiteki/"]Cláudio Henrique[/url].[/p][p]On the audio side, we have added new songs to the game. First, [url="https://www.instagram.com/archiebentoncomposer/"]Archie Benton[/url] start by the Main Theme:[/p][previewyoutube="ug_Vb2gGmjw;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Then he moved to work on the themes for other areas, such as a new theme for the Garden of Earthly Delights:[/p][previewyoutube="BhBJ2Fj-A8w;full"][/previewyoutube][p]There will also be a town that Kalyskah has subdued in the prologue. This is its main theme:[/p][previewyoutube="S1sjHMPBoUQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p]And finally, we have now reached over 35,000 wishlists on Steam!
This means we have hit one of our key milestones, and once the most important systems planned for this year are complete, we will move on to working on the companion system.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/c20489233045bc8e1647e0e3ec9e8d972432244d.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]When will the demo be updated?[/p][p]We have been focusing solely on creating more content for the early access, and even though most of the issues we have on the demo have been fixed on our end, there are a few loose ends that will require us to finish developing other areas before we can update the demo here. So we don’t have an ETA, although it will happen before the Early Access begins.[/p]

notes.title: Prologue Teaser
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
We’re sharing in this video a small glimpse of what you’ll find in the game’s prologue—the story we plan to release once Early Access begins.

There, you will follow Kalyskah at the height of her power, when she controlled vampiric activity across the world, but still found herself stagnated, searching for answers about what to do with her unlife.

I hope you enjoy the little we have to show today!

[previewyoutube=GTxG60bE4GQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Although we still need a few more months, Early Access is getting closer. Expect us to keep you posted as we continue pushing development forward, fixing issues reported in the demo, and implementing new features!

notes.title: What's Next #2
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
I see a lot of new faces following us, so I wanted to give you a glimpse of what’s next for the game. Internally, we’ve had many discussions about our approach to launching in Early Access, so here are a few key topics we’ll be addressing until then:
[h1]When will Early Access start?[/h1]
We plan to launch between June and July, unless we encounter another major issue like we had in the past with the Unreal 5 migration. That is likely our final deadline.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/f0aa22cff6bf36ea007b09000b6c544b6bbd73d8.jpg[/img]
[h1]What will be improved when Early Access begins?[/h1]
We aim to start Early Access on Steam with the prologue content included. The story might not be fully complete, but our goal is to have the introduction quest where Kalyskah speaks with the members of her Legion before the events that led to the fall of her temple. From there, the story progresses up to the point where she performs a ritual in a nearby village, triggering a chain of events that set the stage for her free-roaming adventure. At this point, she will be exploring the island she controls while dealing with pirate factions. So, in short, the first months of Early Access will include both the introduction arc and an early stage of the open-world experience before the Great Fall.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/70edcf0d9375c2df056227aa7141088d737d21b4.jpg[/img]
We also want to refine combat, though we are unsure if we will complete these improvements before or after Early Access begins. The updated combat will feature better animations (including those we recorded with motion capture) and new mechanics that emphasize the build-up of Kalyskah’s excitement during the thrill of the hunt.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/46124de5f04ba49ab645cf44006ced8f386bc6bf.jpg[/img]
All the cutscenes in the current demo are subject to change. However, we might not focus on them right away, as our priority is balancing polish with new content. While we want to offer a great experience, improving animations takes a significant amount of time. At this stage, we believe those efforts would be better spent refining combat animations since fighting is what you will be doing most of the time.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/1bbfc1fcff052f4f644c3ff1c8fa8f8ba7ad02a0.jpg[/img]
The user interface will also be improved. Elements like the health bar, stamina (which, for Kalyskah, is called Vigor Mortis), blood points, and quest navigation are all on our list for enhancements. However, these updates will likely happen during the Early Access phase since our main focus right now is expanding the game’s content to allow for longer playtime.
[h1]Anything about audio?[/h1]
Yes! We are also working on improving the audio. Before The Great Fall, Kalyskah’s world had steampunk-inspired technology, and we plan to add new soundtracks that incorporate metallic vibrations and other elements to reflect that era. This will help differentiate it from the post-fall world.
[previewyoutube=76MEZ-Dwr_s;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]Vampire Roleplay[/h1]
Fully immersing you in the role of a vampire is our highest priority. Many players might be familiar with the personal horror of becoming a monster: the guilt, the fear of losing one’s humanity… But Kalyskah? She has been a vampire for far too long to feel any guilt about her actions. She does not fear becoming a monster; she [b]knows[/b] she is one—and she makes that everyone's problem.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/472dc2540aa63a87046e42ef7da0c26bfba150a1.jpg[/img]
Instead of focusing the narrative internally on her struggles, the game will revolve around her actions and how she interacts with the world. Whether she is compassionate, arrogant, or sadistic is entirely up to the player. But do not worry, you can [i]fix her[/i]! A key part of the story will be about her relationship with humanity and how she chooses to navigate the world that still fears her.
[h1]Romance[/h1]
As I mentioned, Kalyskah is a monster, and she is well aware of it. She sees love as an illusion, an act of pity because everything she touches eventually falls apart. She does not form romantic attachments, nor does she care enough about others to do so. She may flirt, she may toy with emotions, but ultimately, there is a darkness within her that prevents her from feeling true human connection.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/98cae39a981355f9d78b52433b982c7224ddae75.gif[/img]
Most of the time, romance is simply a means to an end—her way of charming people into inviting her into their homes so she can feed on them later. With that in mind, we will be adding relationship mechanics in the future, primarily as a way for Kalyskah to gain favour and build a willing herd. But maybe… just maybe… if you [i]fix her[/i], she might become capable of truly feeling something for someone again.
[h1]The Lore[/h1]
Kalyskah’s world is part of a larger universe we call Night Paths. Throughout the game, you will meet characters who may appear in future projects from our studio. So take notes, we are in this for the long run!


I hope this clears up some of your questions and gets you as excited as we are for the future of the game!

notes.title: Kalyskah Version 0.27.2 & 0.27.3
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
As we continue collecting feedback from Steamfest, these patches focus on fixes and improvements that could be addressed quickly without requiring a major system overhaul. This includes enhancements to combat mechanics, cutscenes, animations, and enemy AI while also laying the groundwork for upcoming difficulty scaling. More updates will follow as we refine additional features based on your feedback.
[previewyoutube=4wue47E0-WE;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed dungeon boss cutscene to improve animations and prevent visual glitches.
[*] Fixed chest simulation physics, making movement more consistent.
[*] Fixed animation slot issues affecting certain weapons and claws.
[*] Fixed clipping in Michael’s glasses and adjusted his outfit.
[*] Fixed NPCs not looking at Kalyskah when expected during interactions.
[*] Fixed UI difficulty settings, ensuring the Steam version does not display the demo level.
[*] Fixed a bug causing game controls to disappear after dialogues—a more complete fix is planned for a future update, since for now we are just brute forcing it to always stay on when outside of cutscenes.
[/list]
[h2]Enhancements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added a tutorial explaining how to block and dodge.
[*] Implemented a new blackboard variable for enemy AI, which will be used to adjust their behaviour based on difficulty settings in future updates.
[*] Increased enemy blocking chance at higher difficulty levels, making combat more dynamic.
[*] Tweaked Michael’s cutscene, improving his body language for more natural animation. We aren't done yet.
[*] Improved animation blending in level sequences, ensuring smoother transitions. We aren't done yet!
[*] Enhanced facial expressions, allowing better animation intensity and independent blinking. There's more to come!
[/list]
[h3]Combat Adjustments[/h3]
[list]
[*] Lowered enemy stamina in Story Mode for a better gameplay balance.
[*] Reduced enemy health scaling per level to smooth out combat progression.
[*] Blood-sucking mechanics updated:
• Parrying enemies before biting them restores less blood compared to sneaking up on them.
• Stealth feeding is now more effective, making it more reliable for eliminating enemies. Notice that if you increase your Sorcery attribute, it will also increase how much blood Kalyskah can take when she bites an enemy.
• Increased overall blood gain, especially when feeding while sneaking.
[*] NPC underwear now matches Kalyskah’s, preventing chest physics and clipping issues.
[/list]
[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some cutscenes still need refinements.
[*] Certain enemy attacks may need further adjustments, particularly after being parried.
[*] Additional UI improvements and difficulty scaling adjustments are planned for future updates.
[/list]
This is just the first wave of fixes based on Steamfest feedback, and we are actively working on further improvements. Keep your feedback coming, and thank you for playing!

notes.title: Kalyskah Version 0.27.1
notes.content:
[h1]Kalyskah Version 0.27.1[/h1]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Resolved null pointer errors and improved index validation in various functions, making the game more stable.
[*] Fixed NPC skill usage and ensured abilities function as intended.
[*] Addressed an issue where Kalyskah wasn’t sprinting correctly.
[*] Corrected logic on the blood-sucking mechanic, ensuring damage starts only when Kalyskah’s teeth make contact.
[*] Fixed UI elements, including interaction button hold functionality, preventing inventory from opening multiple times if you hold the interaction button.
[*] Refined inventory controller detection for gamepads.
[*] Fixed slot description tooltips that do not disappear after closing the menu.
[*] Updated quest-tracking logic to ensure proper progression and eliminate quest-related errors.
[*] Fixed tracked quest UI display issues.
[*] Removed unused and corrupted assets from the project to improve performance.
[*] Fixed Hexblade armour morph targets, resolving issues causing the chest to pop out of the plate mail. Although sometimes it might still happen.
[*] Fixed issues with projectiles, preventing friendly fire and ensuring correct collision behaviour.
[*] Fixed a bug that caused NPCs to repeatedly equip their weapons.
[/list]

[h2]Enhancements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Adjusted cutscenes to prevent clipping, improve transitions, and enhance animations. Not all of them are done yet, we'll release a new patch within the next few days to finish the updates.
[*] Enhanced weapon trails, making them less emissive than before.
[*] Improved HUD elements, including redesigned visuals and better interaction feedback.
[/list]
[h3]Tweaked melee enemy AI:[/h3]
[list]
[*] NPCs now block more reliably.
[*] Enemies will attempt to defend themselves when hit.
[*] Adjusted enemy behaviour to follow Kalyskah more aggressively.
[*] Reduced enemy magic projectile usage to balance melee combat.
[/list]
[h3]Reworked combat animations:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Enemies now start their attacks 40% slower, giving players more time to react before the attack takes full speed. With this change, Kalyskah’s and NPC's attacks feel heavier.
[*] Improved blocking animations, ensuring Kalyskah can move while using a one-handed sword and claws.
[*] Tweaked enemy AI stamina management, affecting how often they attack, block, and reposition.
[*] Updated troll combat: Troll attack speeds have been increased for a more intense challenge.
[*] Updated archer AI:
[*] Archers now telegraph their shots before firing.
[*] They will no longer fire if they lack a line of sight.
[*] They now walk instead of sprinting away when repositioning.
[/list]
[h3]Reworked ranged combat mechanics:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved visuals on spider projectiles.
[*] Reduced arrow speeds for better reaction time.
[*] Fixed projectiles colliding with the world properly, preventing spells from stopping midair as well.
[*] Added visual and sound cues for parrying: Attacks now have improved feedback, helping players identify when enemies are vulnerable.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/f280b0c2b33d0fdf60d7c362be823aed867f8fa2.jpg[/img]
[h3]Improved blood-sucking mechanics:[/h3]
[list]
[*] After a successful parry, the player can hold the interaction button to bite an enemy.
[*] Kalyskah now turns into mist before teleporting behind enemies, then returns to where she was. This should prevent her from clipping through walls after sneaking behind enemies or biting them in combat.
[*] Reduced slow-motion effects during feeding.
[*] Adjusted combat biting balance, reducing blood recovered to compensate for its increased accessibility.
[*] Stealth bites now deal increased damage and players can see Kalyskah's stats while doing it. 
[/list]
[h3]Cutscene improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted Alvina’s cutscene for better narrative flow.
[*] Improved Michael’s cutscene animations and dialogue.
[*] Enhanced lighting and visual transitions in key scenes.
[/list]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Enabled biting during combat: Players can now parry an enemy attack and bite them in the recovery window.
[*] Introduced new HUD rework (V1): The UI has been overhauled to improve clarity and functionality.
[*] Updated NPC combat behaviour: NPCs will now react more dynamically based on their stamina.
[*] Overhauled projectile system: Projectiles are now less likely to collide with each other, ensuring smoother-ranged combat.
[*] The plate armour that the Seekers use is now available to be found at the goblin mine, and we split its slots a bit better to allow players to mix them with different clothing.
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some visual glitches persist in less optimised areas of the open world—additional HLOD passes are planned.
[*] Certain NPC animations and interactions may require minor refinements in future updates.
[*] The updated plate armour may cause incompatibilities with old saves, leading to missing items.
[*] Animations such as the one that plays when Kalyskah defeats Greemnoch is under development, and they aren't looking as polished as the others (there's a wall missing).
[/list]

notes.title: Character Profile: Ilreth Baequianea
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=8BR4H4rfjS0;full][/previewyoutube]
Paraphrasing, we could describe Ilreth as:
[i]"Abstractions like justice don’t mean much to her. She’s loyal to people, not to principles. And she expects loyalty in return. She would stop at nothing to save a friend, for example, because she believes they would do the same for her."
Paraphrasing Matthew Woodring Stover in Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (2005)[/i]

Ilreth is an extremely loyal person, but also completely fanatic when it comes to protecting the ones she cares about, having no moral compass to stop her from doing the most heinous crimes if it's to save a beloved one.

So let’s dive into the life of one of the most complicated and morally ambiguous characters in Kalyskah lore:

[h1]Early Life[/h1]
The high-elf Ilreth Baequianea was born in the kingdom of Danú in the year 10,860 Before Fionn, according to the Dragonian Calendar of her world. Meaning that she wasn’t much more than 300 years old when the Prologue story happens in Kalyskah.
For centuries, her family coexisted with a nearby human village. The elves often hosted extravagant balls, grand dinners, and lively festivals, offering the humans a glimpse of their opulence and sharing moments of joy. Despite this generosity, the humans harboured deep-seated envy towards the elves' wealth and seemingly eternal lives. One night, consumed by greed, they conspired to raid the estate. In their desperation to seize the elves' riches, they murdered Ilreth's parents.
Still a young girl, Ilreth was spared thanks to the intervention of an elvish count named Elrand, who was visiting her parents' home that night. The king of Danú exacted harsh punishment upon the humans responsible, reclaiming the lands they had stolen. However, there was little left for Ilreth to return to. The castle she called home had been reduced to ashes, and though she inherited a significant amount of gold, it could not replace her family or the lifestyle she had lost.
Elrand took Ilreth under his care, bringing her to Lindara, the elven capital in the neighbouring kingdom of Bourges. The pain of her loss festered into a deep hatred for humanity and in Lindara, a city where humans were often treated as little more than servants, labourers, or even slaves, only deepened her disdain. To Ilreth, humans were a flawed and inferior race, unworthy of the generosity her family had shown.
Amidst the grandeur of Lindara, Ilreth discovered a passion for magical artefacts. She became particularly fascinated by the Iathori Crystalas, powerful gems that fuelled the city’s magical energy, and the many wonderful and enchanted items crafted by elven artisans.
Despite her growing disdain for humankind, she enjoyed the company of dwarves and other beings.  While their lifespans were brief compared to the near-eternity granted to elves, their perspectives and ingenuity would instil her to ask questions and continue her amateurish researches about such objects.
[h2]Adulthood and another taste of human greed[/h2]
When Ilreth came of age, she used her inheritance, combined with additional support from Elrand, to enrol in Lindara's Magic Academy. There, she refined her skills and advanced swiftly as an artificer, blending the structured knowledge of the academy with the practical insights she had gained from dwarven craftsmen.
After completing her initial studies, Ilreth quickly earned a reputation as a rising talent among artificers, crafting artefacts such as her own gauntlet and amulet, which shielded her from physical harm. However, her ambition extended far beyond simple mastery. She aspired to join the University’s prestigious inner circle, a position reserved for those whose research redefined the boundaries of their craft. To achieve this, Ilreth needed to produce groundbreaking work that would surpass all expectations. Despite her disdain for humanity, she recognised the necessity of venturing beyond Lindara's familiar confines. Setting aside her pride in favour of intellectual curiosity, she began travelling the wider world, seeking inspiration and knowledge wherever it could be found, even in human lands.
At 300 years old, in the year of 10.560 BF, her travels led her to the kingdom now known as Three Wolves, where she became embroiled in the devastating conflict sparked by a red dragon named Vassíris. Raised by silver dragons and accepted as one of their own, Vassíris seemed destined for a peaceful life among his adoptive kin. However, his story took a dark turn when he fell in love with a human. Ambitious and power-hungry, a group of humans sought to exploit the dragon’s blood for a ritual. Using his lover as bait, they lured Vassíris into a trap, successfully completing their ritual at the cost of the human’s life. Though Vassíris escaped, the way humans used someone he loved to trap him and perform the ritual shattered him.
Grimm’Arch, the silver dragon who had raised Vassíris and served as the leader of the dragons, urged him to forgive the humans and move on. Enraged by the plea for mercy, Vassíris turned on his adoptive father, killing Grimm in a fit of fury. His actions ignited a war that would fracture the unity of the dragons. Vassíris declared his intention to enslave all non-draconic races—humans, elves, and any other beings he deemed lesser. In response, Grimm's son, Bill’Arch, rose to challenge Vassíris, leading a faction of dragons who sought to protect the humanoid races from annihilation.
The escalating conflict divided the dragonkind into bitter factions, with some supporting Vassíris' vendetta and others aligning with Bill’Arch and the silver dragons who championed coexistence. The chaos engulfed the lands of Danú, spreading destruction across kingdoms. Witnessing the devastation and recognising the futility of remaining amidst such strife, Ilreth seized the opportunity to flee. Cloaking her departure in the guise of furthering her research, she left the continent entirely, driven by both fear and ambition. Her journey ultimately led her to Thulgatha, a land steeped in ancient ruins, forgotten knowledge, and artefacts of immense power, where she hoped to uncover secrets that would solidify her place among the greatest artificers of her age.
[h1]Travelling to Thulgatha[/h1]
Upon arriving in Thulgatha, Ilreth was startled to discover that the majority of the population was human. Despite their greed and what she regarded as the filthiness of their ways, she grudgingly acknowledged that they were far more civilised and technologically advanced than the people of her homeland. During her travels, she encountered a peculiar man who called himself Michael the Wise. Unlike most humans, Michael possessed an unusual awareness of time, akin to the elves' eternal sensitivity to its passage. He understood the value of patience and craftsmanship, qualities that earned Ilreth’s respect.
Michael revealed that he worked for a woman named Kalyskah Karnstein, the owner of a university in Thulgatha. He invited Ilreth to collaborate on his research into the Iathori Crystalas, or as the people of Thulgatha called them, "Star Crystals." During her time there, Ilreth uncovered truths about the crystals, learning that they originated from the stars and that they were tied to a plane called The Primal Earth. However, her work was frequently disrupted by the tumultuous environment of the university. Most shocking was the discovery that Kalyskah and Michael, along with many of the university’s other members, were vampires. She had long talks with a vampire named Laver, a fellow elf about the stars and elven origins, but back then, they were still strangers.
Ilreth was offered the opportunity to become a vampire herself but refused. As an elf, her immortality rendered such a transformation unnecessary, and she found the idea unappealing. Nonetheless, she was unfazed by the cruelty of the vampires and even used her time among them to release some of her lingering hatred toward humans, particularly when the vampires sacrificed them to a beast called Gremmnoch.
Drawing on the knowledge she gained during her time with the vampires, Ilreth discovered that the Star Crystals could be used to travel between worlds. With Michael’s assistance, she devised an elaborate method to harness their power for interdimensional travel, testing it first on animals. Guided by her unrelenting curiosity, she eventually learned that all worlds are mere reflections of an original plane known as Primal Earth.
Obsessed with understanding how the crystals connected to this first world, Ilreth began organising an expedition. However, her plans were thrown into chaos when Kalyskah’s university…… Oh, sorry about stopping here. You’ll learn what happens next in the prologue 😉 

[h1]Combat Strategy[/h1]
Ilreth wields her powers intertwining her intellect with subtle supernatural abilities, that even though aren’t match to the innate magic vampires have, still allows her to be a threat to her foes. Her mastery over crafting artefacts ensures that, planning ahead, she is usually prepared for any situation. Each artefact she creates reflects her magic’s visceral nature, bleeding with primal energy and exuding a mixture of elven and dwarven craft. She never leaves home without four key artefacts: one for protection, one for active violence, one for escape, and a fourth tailored to her current needs.
Her signature weapon is a scythe filled with runes, enchanted to drain the vitality of her foes, allowing her to fuel her magic without risk. Though not skilled with weapons, her unnatural dexterity and quick reflexes make her a formidable combatant. Despite her capability to handle threats, Ilreth prefers to avoid combat altogether. Her cadence of speech and  somewhat diplomatic approach when she recognizes someone is a threat, helps her resolve situations before violence becomes necessary. 
Ilreth’s approach to conflict has evolved over time. Back when she started studying with Amara, the Enlightened of the Storm of Death, she used enchanted gems to reanimate corpses as zombies. But as necromancy grew politically dangerous, she adapted her methods. Now, when brute force becomes unavoidable, she crafts stone golems using the same principles of adding a crystal as their core. 
Her innate elven magic, boosted by her studies as an artificer, allows her to transform objects and environments to her advantage by hitting whatever she wants to transmute with her tools. Her artefacts amplify her abilities, creating subtle manipulations and environmental traps that leave enemies at a disadvantage.
Her strategies are calculated and layered, focusing on anticipating threats and planning ahead so she can precisely manipulate the outcomes. Ilreth views conflict not as a test of strength but as a game of strategy to dominate the battlefield. Her ruthlessness fuels her work, ensuring her allies are prepared and her enemies are outmatched.

notes.title: Happy Christmas!
notes.content:
We all wish you a Happy Christmas and hope your dreams come true, the same way you are helping our dream become reality!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/1c718f1128fcaf14a5a5175d1b3582ff8b05045d.jpg[/img]

This year brought some major setbacks as we transitioned the game to Unreal 5. The lesson we learned this year was patience. As things started to complicate in the new engine, we took a deep breath and assessed what was wrong. Realising we were building a house on sand; we stepped back and started reworking from the basics. We conducted countless tests, implemented new ideas, and explored the technologies that would work versus those that wouldn’t. Then, we went back and redid features using what we’d learned, all that while trying our best to ship version 0.26 in time for Halloween! 

We still have a lot of ground to cover until the game reaches the polish we want so we can officially start the early access, but here’s some of what you can expect:

We managed to hire an amazing level designer who guided us in improving performance by reworking our shaders, adjusting the level of detail of our assets, and implementing technologies to load the world in smaller chunks.

We also brought on someone new who will be working on different variations of Kalyskah’s soundtrack next year. Our programmer has created a branch from the main project to rework the base classes. On the animation side, we travelled to another area here in Brazil to motion capture the cutscene, and we’re now polishing it using Unreal’s proper workflow. This involves a rig that allows us to animate cutscenes directly in the engine, rather than constantly bouncing back and forth with Blender.

And there’s so much more. I can’t express how happy I am to see that, through all this tortuous path, you stayed by our side, offering feedback and ideas for the game. Many of your suggestions have been noted and will be implemented once the refactoring is complete.
As we finish reworking the game’s foundation, we’ll return to implementing new features and building the a storyline that bridges Kalyskah before the fall of her temple, and the current state you see her legion at the demo. 

Thank you so much for your support! Kalyskah is more than a game to us—it’s a project we’ve poured our hearts into because it’s the medieval vampire game with erotic elements that we always wanted to play. Having people like you backing us and helping to make this dream a reality gives us the strength to push through sleepless nights and endless research—with a smile on our faces!

Once again, have a wonderful Christmas and an amazing New Year!

notes.title: What's next for Kalyskah?
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
We are delighted to say that we passed the 20k wishlist milestone! 🎉
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/d2ccdcdb562fa0b98cc6e4212f08a737ea076c58.jpg[/img]
But work doesn't end there, we are just getting started!

[h2]Prologue[/h2]
In the game's trailer, you might have noticed that Kalyskah is an open-world game and that we have much more content completed than what is shown in the demo. The demo represents the first step in our conversion of the game to Unreal 5, as we originally began development in Unreal 4. During this process, we improved the landscape, but some elements became misaligned from their original positions, and we are currently addressing these issues in the cutscenes. Our goal is to update the demo next year to provide a glimpse of what we aim to achieve for the open world, where you will explore the world before Kalyskah's temple fell into ruins.
This is a preview of what we are doing so far; we'll be adding nanite, balancing the colours and making many other improvements before it's ready:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/df093b10b75401c975b96bb0a8ec9aaa331b04ec.jpg[/img]

[h2]The Imp:[/h2]

[h2]The Interface[/h2]

I hope you are as excited as we are to see where this vampire story will go, cheers! 🩸

notes.title: Steam Demo!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 
We’re thrilled to share the first demo of our game here on Steam!
The road so far has been filled with challenges. The idea of creating a game like Kalyskah has been in our hearts for a long time and what you see now is just a small glimpse of what we envision for the future.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/ea13e203cf5e70e6bc7646817192b87fd9763389.jpg[/img]

There’s much more to come, including an open world to explore and a variety of immersive systems that will let you experience life as a creature of the night, hiding your true nature from human society.
This demo offers a brief look at Kalyskah’s journey, covering some of the events between the opening and the first arc of the story. It should provide around 30 minutes of gameplay, followed by a short group of dialogues with some of the characters you'll encounter in the full game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/939d6b25b053a849c0759f882fbf87d45f2cb45d.jpg[/img]

Early next week, we plan to release another dungeon, featuring more platforming for you to explore.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/cd4823a56b209ab657633c59da3ac2a9e913ddaf.jpg[/img]

Since switching from Unreal 4 to Unreal 5, we’ve had to patch many systems and haven’t yet had the time to rework most of them. So, everything you see here is still subject to improvement, especially the combat and animations!

Have a great day and I hope you have fun!

notes.title: Meet our VAs - Amy Saville, Kalyskah herself!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
Amy has been with us since the very start of the project, and she’s not just an amazing person but also an incredibly talented actress! She knows Kalyskah’s personality and journey inside out, so this video will give you a better insight into her work and offer hints about Kalyskah’s character.
[previewyoutube=Tr25Pc1PHd4;full][/previewyoutube]

Talking a bit more about Kalyskah as a character, she starts the game as a villainous vampire, viewing "the living" as nothing more than cattle, an expendable mass she uses for her own gain. Despite this, she has no interest in ruling over them or becoming an empress. From this starting point, much will unfold, and you’ll be able to shape her growth as a character. Whether that leads her deeper into her disdain for "the living" or towards a path of compassion and altruism.

Selfishness and altruism lie at the unbeating heart of many of the choices you’ll make throughout her journey. But it’s important to remember that bad things can happen to good people, and the most compassionate decisions won’t always lead to better outcomes in the long run. Learning to navigate this world is what makes Kalyskah’s choices feel so significant and unique.

Kalyskah is old—ancient, even. She’s lived so long that she’s lost track of the millennia she’s walked this earth. Love is the last thing she seeks. Cunning and manipulative, she can still be warm at times, occasionally displaying a crude sense of humour. At the start of the game, she’s fiercely loyal to her cause and her people, adept in sorcery, but terrible with a sword. And her development in both personal and technical areas of her life will be heavily influenced by your choices!

notes.title: Meet our Voice Actors - Lucas Webley
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
We are delighted to introduce Lucas Webley, the talented voice behind characters such as James, Laver, shopkeepers, an orc, and many more in our game. Without further ado, let’s hand the microphone over to him:
[previewyoutube=p7C09mbXfW0;full][/previewyoutube]

As a little addition to what Lucas mentioned, James is not exactly Kalyskah's [i]romantic[/i] love interest. As the monster she is, Kalyskah has no interest in love—at least not in the romantic sense. James is an important newly-turned vampire, and she will be mentoring him and engaging with his dilemma as he struggles with his new undead nature. He will serve as a cornerstone that connects Kalyskah to her humanity, often offering his perspective when Kalyskah indulges too deeply in her hunger and edges dangerously close to viewing humans solely as food or tools to further her ambitions.

On the other hand, Laver represents the opposite. He is the devilish whisperer, an elder vampire from her Karnstein Legion, who constantly reminds her of the superiority of their kind. Knowing her full potential and power, Laver will tempt her with notions that, without her leadership, humans are doomed to walk towards inevitable ruin.

Thank you for reading, and we hope you enjoy Kalyskah's journey as much as we are enjoying bringing it to you!
Our next post here might either be answers to questions that you have for the voice actresses or a deeper gaze into the vampire mythos we're using in the game.

Until next time, take care!

notes.title: The World of Kalyskah
notes.content:
Welcome to [i]Kalyskah[/i], where we are blending the timeless gothic temptation of vampiric tales with an immersive RPG experience. We recently updated our old Unreal 4 prototype to Unreal 5 and our team is now focusing on our first demo. Even though it will be small, we want to ensure that it will be polished enough to be shown on Steam.

[h1]The World of Kalyskah[/h1]
[i]Kalyskah[/i] is set in Thulgatha, an ancient land inspired by the rugged and mystical landscapes of the Balkans. Here, towering mountains rise above the clouds, and ancient forests hide secrets long forgotten. This is a fantasy world, one where the supernatural is ever-present, where different races, each with their histories and struggles, coexist in a fragile balance.
Players will guide Kalyskah through two distinct eras, defined by events before and after The Great Fall. In the prologue, you will experience a society thriving on steam and gears, where technology drives progress, and the Karnstein Legion dominates every human on Tupelo's island. However, a pivotal event drives Kalyskah into a deep slumber, and while she sleeps, the world is irrevocably altered by a cataclysmic event.
When Kalyskah awakens a long time later, she finds herself in a world that has moved on without her—a world where the remnants of the old mechanical society have been transformed by new technologies that harness magic in ways she never imagined. The contrast between the steampunk past and the blend of magic and medieval that dominates the present offers a unique journey where ruins might seem more modern than the world around Kalyskah.
But these changing landscapes are merely the background for a narrative driven by choice and consequence. Kalyskah’s journey is deeply personal and shaped by the decisions you make. Will she embrace the darkness within her, becoming a monster feared by all? Or will she find a way to balance her power with compassion, using her abilities to protect rather than dominate? The path she takes will determine the fate of Thulgatha and her new legacy.

[h2]Magic[/h2]
Magic in the world of [i]Kalyskah[/i] is ancient and mysterious. Some scholars believe it originates from The Storms, raw forces of creation that predate even the gods. Others argue that magic is tied to the very fabric of reality, with each aspect of existence resonating with these primordial forces. The truth is a matter of debate for scholars, but what is clear is that magic has become far more prevalent in the world following the events of The Great Fall.
Most magic in Thulgatha is wielded through tools and artefacts, with only a few individuals possessing the innate ability to channel it directly. The presence of magic has shifted the balance of power, creating new opportunities and new dangers.

[h1]Vampires and Vampirism[/h1]
Humans are the most populous race in Thulgatha and form the backbone of its civilizations. The Great Fall destroyed the age of prosperity and technology that humanity created, forcing them back to the Stone Age; however, ever adaptable, humanity endured and recovered. They are the survivors, the builders, and the dreamers, navigating a world filled with both old threats and new opportunities.
Vampires in [i]Kalyskah[/i] are not just undead—they are beings of immense power, beauty, and complexity. Vampirism is a curse that can affect any being, be they human, elf, or orc. This transformation doesn’t just change their nature; it amplifies their abilities, making them stronger and more formidable than they ever were, and the effects only intensify with age.
As the first vampire, Kalyskah possesses incredible powers, and she extends these Dark Gifts to her cursed progeny. These abilities set them further apart from Humans, allowing them to dominate them with ease. However, Vampires still need to be careful. With tens of thousands of Humans for every Vampire, they are hopelessly outnumbered. And just like the wolf does not reveal its presence to the sheep, so too do Vampires live in secrecy, lest they provoke a violent response from their food. Indeed, previous abuses have already led to the creation of organisations that hunts the undead. Known as the Seekers, these Humans are trained to combat Vampires and are a threat only ignored by short-lived fools.
[h2]Kalyskah’s Internal Conflict[/h2]
Kalyskah’s beauty is as much a weapon as her strength. She knows how to use her immortal allure and charisma to get what she wants, bending the world to her will, and at the heart of our game is her internal struggle and how she uses these tools to achieve her goals—a battle between her vampiric nature and the remnants of her humanity. Kalyskah begins her journey as a powerful yet deeply flawed character. She is initially selfish and controlling, driven by a desire to build a legacy that will endure eternity at any cost. 
The player’s choices will directly influence how Kalyskah navigates her world and who she becomes—whether she embraces her darker instincts or finds a way to retain some semblance of empathy towards the living. Almost every quest will have alternate endings or different approaches depending on how compassionate and loyal Kalyskah is to her Legion.
[h2]Vampiric Traits and Facts[/h2]
Vampires in [i]Kalyskah[/i] are complex beings, each one shaped by the unique circumstances of their transformation and the bloodline from which they descend. The game delves deeply into the lore of vampirism, offering players a rich tapestry of myths, facts, and unique traits that define what it means to be a vampire in Thulgatha. A few of the first interactions you will have will showcase the world we are building:
[list]
[*] [b]Bloodlines and Gifts:[/b] Vampires can develop unique abilities known as "Dark Gifts," which are passed down through bloodlines. For example, Laver, one of Kalyskah’s primogens, can move with such speed that it appears as though he is teleporting. As the original, Kalyskah is capable of developing the abilities of every single bloodline, but first, she needs to have a taste of the blood of her children.
[*] [b]Eye Colours and Lineage:[/b] The colour of a vampire’s eyes can reveal much about their lineage and power. Kalyskah, as the first vampire, is the only one who has red eyes. Vampires she directly turns typically have orange eyes, signifying their close connection to her. As the bloodline dilutes, the eye colours shift, with vampires further removed from Kalyskah exhibiting more natural hues. However, those with exceptional magical potential might awaken with blue eyes, marking them as unique even among their peers​.
[*] [b]Myths vs. Reality:[/b] The game also explores common myths about vampires, separating fact from fiction. While many of these myths were spread by the Seekers, who don't fully understand the twists in the blood, some hold a kernel of truth. For instance, while vampires do need to drink blood to sustain themselves, they can also derive sustenance from other life-related fluids. Additionally, while sunlight is harmful, it is not instantly fatal—older, well-fed vampires can withstand it, though it drains their strength and abilities​.
[/list]
As Kalyskah, players will navigate a world that both reveres and fears her. She is a figure of legend, known for her ruthlessness and power, but also for the darkness that she embodies. This reputation allows her to command respect, but it also makes her a target for those who seek to control or destroy her.

[h1]Exploration and Atmosphere[/h1]
Thulgatha is not just a backdrop for the story; it is a character in its own right, with each location offering its own mood, challenges, and secrets. From the peaks of Millhaven to the dense, ancient forests that conceal forgotten ruins, the world is designed to draw players in, encouraging exploration and rewarding those who seek out its hidden corners.
The game’s atmosphere is enhanced by its detailed world-building, with every location reflecting the history and events that have shaped it. Whether it’s the remnants of the advanced societies of old or the new, magical elements that have emerged after The Great Fall, each area tells its own story, adding artefacts to be found and hidden lore to be uncovered.

[h1]Looking Ahead[/h1]
As we continue to develop [i]Kalyskah[/i], our focus remains on delivering a game that is not only visually stunning but also rich in narrative depth and gameplay variety. We are a small team, but we are committed to ensuring that every aspect of the game, from the smallest environmental detail to the overarching plot, reflects the world we have created—a world that is as dark and seductive as it is dangerous. Your support during the Early Access period will greatly help us bring this vision to reality, increase our numbers, and realise the game as we conceived it.
We hope you enjoy what will be available in the demo that we’ll be releasing to Steam soon. We are excited to share more about this wonderful and dark world as we continue to realise our vision for this project, and we hope you’ll come along with us on this journey.

Happy hunt!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/69c5a3012073fa2a9983fdff8b70f4aae768bac4.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Moving to Unreal Engine 5 and Upcoming Demo Delay
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
Not many of you might know that we started to develop the game in Unreal 4, and for the past months, we've been bringing it to Unreal 5. This is one of the big reasons why we have a very big message in our trailers saying that what you see there, is not the final looks of the game.

The problem is that there were plugins and other features that we used in Unreal 4 that started to cause errors (Especially in the back-end C++ code) and we had to update them manually to the new standards of Unreal 5. These errors accumulated and we have worked really hard to try and catch them in time for the Steamfest, but unfortunately, we will need more time.

We won't be able to release a demo during June's Steamfest, but as soon as we can, we will come back to give you a new ETA for an out-of-season demo.

On the bright side, with more time, while our programmers are attacking on the source-code front to fix the issues, the other team members will bring improvements on animations, level design and perhaps we can even slide in some new outfits for when we do bring you a new release, it will have more content than what was originally intended for this month.

Thank you very much for your patience!

notes.title: What to expect from our demo on Steamfest?
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
We’re hard at work getting a demo ready for the Steamfest in June. It aims to showcase the ideas we’re bringing to the table rather than being the final version of the mechanics you will find in Kalyskah. Still, I want to go over what you can expect:

[h1]Story[/h1]
Our game is split into two eras: Prologue and Main-Story. During the prologue, you will control Kalyskah at the height of her power. The main story, on the other hand, starts when she wakes up in a world that no longer remembers her. With her power stored in a Blood Idol, she must start from scratch and rebuild everything she’s lost.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/411ba0be7bb6c0aad580c8a59007df5e92714add.png[/img]
The demo will be brief but it should be enough to hint at the major plot points of the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/5de44db629ce98f3831b5ccc67d3fbfe42f63ffe.png[/img]

[h1]Side Content[/h1]
The demo will also have a place called The Garden of Earthly Delights, run by a friendly but mysterious woman called Nemesis. 
[previewyoutube=bY96YZLeibU;full][/previewyoutube]
This is a place between realities where Kalysakh can sate both her lust and bloodlust.
Keep in mind that our base game doesn't have explicit nudity or sexual content. However, you can unlock this content by using our [b]free DLC[/b]. Unfortunately, since you won’t be able to activate DLCs on demos during Steamfest, this content will not be available for now. Also, some countries, such as Germany and China, block this kind of content altogether, so we won’t be able to distribute the DLC through Steam in these regions.

[h1]Combat[/h1]
The demo won't contain the final and brutal vision we have for this vampire game. We’ve motion-captured new animations, but they will not be ready by June, so we’ll use placeholders for this demo. Here's a teaser of what we’ll be working with later this year.
[previewyoutube=J5JiBxh4vXw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]RPG[/h1]
Ours is a roleplaying game, and we want to make you feel like you’re living on the skin of this classic vampire. You’ll be able to harness the gifts of the blood to accomplish supernatural feats and dominate your foes. However, not everything is great for a vampire. You’ll have to deal with the weaknesses that come with your condition, such as garlic, the need for an invitation to get inside homes, the lack of a reflection and everything that makes Bram Stoker vampires shine. On top of that, you’ll need to blend in among the flock, hiding your true nature from those you seek to feed from and the hunters that would see you destroyed. The choices you make will not only shape Kalyskha’s disposition towards humans, but also influence how the world sees her.
Most of these parts of the game are still a work-in-progress and we don’t feel like they are polished enough to be shown at an event as big as Steamfest. But we have added a few dialogues with choices so you can have an idea of how this system will work in the future. Will she forever remain the self-centred and arrogant cult leader, or will she understand that humans, despite being fragile, should be cherished and respected? The choice is yours.

notes.title: We Reached 10 Thousand Wishlists!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
Thank you for all that added our game to their wishlist!
We hit 10 thousand! Reaching this [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1818660/view/5319372434960809480]milestone[/url] we can have a better projection of how our budget will expand and allow us to increase the planned content for sidequests and interactions in the open world!

We are planning on running a poll for which character we'll be adding to the game based on your feedback, but given some thought, we realised that there's no better way to do it than when we have a demo for you to feel first hand the world we are creating and envision who you'd like us to add there. Still, don't be afraid to post here in the comments your ideas, we are collecting them to better tailor this character based on things you'd like to see in our game!


And if you haven't yet, remember to wishlist Kalyskah on Steam!

notes.title: [News] Overview of the plans for 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,
This year will be the most important one so far on Kalyskah’s development and we’d like to acknowledge that we wouldn’t be here if it wasn’t for all the supporters and fans who stood by us for these trying years, thank you for believing and supporting us.

With that in mind, we’d like to remain transparent with the community and share our plan for this year and what it will mean for the Kalyskah game.
The big event of the year for us will be the Early Access release, and with that in mind, we’ve made big structural changes within the team, we are now focusing all our resources on making sure we deliver a stable, fun and optimized experience for everyone when they click play on the Early Access release day.

Also throughout the year we will be participating in numerous events, both online and live and for that, we are working on a new public demo, this will have restricted areas until all the code is updated but will allow players to have a taste of what the game will be like on Unreal 5 when it releases. The demo and all the pre-alpha versions will still be available for supporters during production.

[h1]Quarterly Timeline[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/43208b5dd64b8ecece844c475ea338e70ddd8717.gif[/img]
[h2]Q1 - Unreal 5[/h2]
[list]
[*] Kalyskah Demo.
[*] Technical work on the Unreal 5 transition.
[*] Update the game trailer (Both Story and Erotic Content).
[*] CDQ Belo Horizonte - Showing Kalyskah’s Statue.
[/list]
[h2]Q2 - Polishing[/h2]
[list]
[*] Game optimization and polish.
[*] Steam fest.
[/list]
[h2]Q3 - Ealy Access[/h2]
[list]
[*] EA release.
[*] New Trailer with Unreal 5.
[/list]
[h2]Q4 - Events[/h2]
[list]
[*] Bug fixing and polish.
[*] BGS (Brasil Game Show) - Showing Kalyskah’s Statue.
[*] Comic-Con Experience (Brazil) - Showing Kalyskah’s Statue.
[/list]
[h1]Teams[/h1]
[h2]Technical Team[/h2]
First quarter the technical team will finish the conversion to Unreal 5, this entails fitting the old data to new systems, fixing errors on the map and reviewing all the assets.
The second quarter will be a mix of continuing the work with readying the demo and other presentation elements.
The rest of the year will be system development focused and polish and testing for EA release.
[h2]Voice Actors[/h2]
During 2024 the voice actors will focus on ambient dialog and banter to liven up the world. As cinematics will be reduced, long dialogues will not be as often.
[h2]Animators[/h2]
Will focus on ambient animation and object interaction throughout the world. When the Unreal 5 conversion is done, animators will focus on the combat overhaul along with the technical team. 
In Q3, Animators will help polish the game and add missing animations to the quests and cinematics.
[h2]Writers[/h2]
New quests will be on pause until we finish UE5 transition and prepare the new systems for the open world,  quests will be resumed in Q2 and voiced according to the available budget.
[h2]Art[/h2]
The modellers will keep focus on the characters, implementing new clothes and hair.


Best wishes,
[b]Nobre Lobo[/b] team!

And thank you for the over 8500 wishlists so far, we are close to the next milestone!

notes.title: Clothes and Cloth-tag system in Kalyskah!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
Today I wanted to show you some of the outfits that you will be able to find on the game, together with an explanation of our cloth tags!

The first cloth we have here is the one that a character called Ilreth wears:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/8b6739878ce634b65e76e2e26c228f3e8ad5969e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/143d5f136cb94d87059b64355ed58562ba4f0dba.png[/img]

And the second here what a succubus called Nemesis will wear on the first time Kalyskah meets her:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/1705d57a4d6a53996bc20ddb53ed7df9975a647f.png[/img]


While designing outfits, our goal is to have them ranging from fully armoured, elegant, and even enticing and revealing designs. Your choice of attire will affect some of the quests that you find, changing or unlocking dialogue options and having NPCs react to the way Kalyskah presents herself. All that is done by our tag system.

Is your Kalyskah a vampire who wants to easily intimidate people and cast fear in people's hearts? Wear clothes with the [i]menacing[/i] tag. But should her prefer a smoother approach, and tempt her possible allies or victims into giving what she wants by arousing their desires, she can wear clothes with the [i]enticing[/i] tag. These tags are not mutually exclusive, because well, sometimes she can bee both seductive and intimidating!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/4fb488dc73788df072ba4398b56c9e42d3be80da.png[/img]

You may also find re-playable events in the world that require you to try your luck on talking your way out of some situations, like when bandits approach Kalyskah. Her cloth tags can influence the chance of success depending on what is her approach. For example, when Kalyskah is wearing her heavy armour, she gets the meaning tag, and this can increase her chances of success on intimidation but reduces her chances of seduction:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44699620/c5b08ec586804a1cbd7d47bb81866be30b1c9e07.png[/img]

But don't think that all is lost just because you chosen a certain attire, and that your choices are locked in a certain path, these stats can also be influenced by your attributes and luck, and as long as there's an opportunity to use a certain stat, there is always a chance!
